rules.title: No emoji in source, docs or UI
rules.statement: Source, documentation and UI copy contain no pictographic emoji; UI surface files also use inline SVG rather than icon-like text characters.

rules.title: Canonical tool schema is validated before dispatch
rules.statement: Every model tool call is decoded strictly and validated against the tool's canonical JSON Schema in Tool.parameters before it executes; a provider grammar or structured-output mode never replaces that local check.

rules.title: Registered tool contracts are certifiable and spec-consistent
rules.statement: Every registered Tool has a unique provider-safe name, a reviewed description, a certifiable object schema and a spec() that matches the canonical registered values.

rules.title: Approval and permission boundaries change deliberately
rules.statement: An execution boundary changes only with an explicit task, focused tests for allowed, ask and deny paths, and documentation of the new boundary; no feature widens authority incidentally.

checklist: The task names who approves what, for which Bot and account, and which data moves
New or changed effects route through the existing policy engine, approval gate and action receipt
Focused tests cover allowed, ask (pauses then resumes) and deny paths, and docs name the boundary change

rules.title: Local-first routing and secret handling are preserved
rules.statement: Prompts, files and tool output leave the machine only through a provider route the user configured, and secrets or private account data never enter client artifacts, logs or receipts.

checklist: No new credential class, secret or private account data enters a client artifact, transcript or log
Hosted routes are used only when the Bot's routing and the owner's configuration allow them
Tools that accept transient secrets override Tool.recorded_arguments before anything is persisted

rules.title: 400-line source cap and shrink-only baseline
rules.statement: A new source file stays at or below 400 lines; over-cap files are frozen in .file-size-baseline.json and may shrink but never grow, with splits landing at 350-400 lines.

rules.title: Quiet focused validation is the default inner loop
rules.statement: Agents run focused, quiet checks and the default gate instead of full suites, Playwright or native builds unless the change warrants escalation stated in the task.

rules.title: Generated CSS is built from sources, never hand-edited
rules.statement: The generated ui.css, model-switcher.css, app.css and styles.min.css files are outputs of app/src and website sources; edits happen in the sources and are rebuilt with npm run build:css.

checklist: ui.css, model-switcher.css, app.css and styles.min.css were not hand-edited
CSS changes were made in app/src/ or website/ sources and rebuilt with npm run build:css
The report says whether build:css ran or why it was unnecessary

rules.title: Commits carry no AI-tool attribution
rules.statement: Commit messages, trailers and signatures contain no AI-tool attribution, generated-by marker or bot co-author; the maintainer authors commits.

checklist: No AI-tool attribution trailer, generated-by signature or bot co-author appears in the commit
The staged diff and final git status were reviewed before reporting the change

rules.title: Runtime state, fixtures and reviewed evidence stay out of commits
rules.statement: Runtime state, credentials, SQLite sidecars, generated output and reviewed evidence follow .gitignore; fixtures and evidence are intentional inputs and are never blindly added, pruned or untracked.

rules.title: Persisted state uses pydantic models, ordered migrations and UTC ISO timestamps
rules.statement: Persisted state is modeled in models.py, schema changes use a new ordered SQLite migration in store.py, and timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC via models.iso/models.utcnow rather than naive local time.

rules.title: Focused regression tests accompany behaviour changes
rules.statement: Each behaviour change ships with focused pytest coverage run through npm run test:agent with explicit paths, so the quiet lane exercises the changed seam.

rules.title: External agent tooling is pinned, sandboxed and verified
rules.statement: MCP servers and code-graph or other external agent tools enter the harness only with explicit approval, a pinned version or commit, sandboxed access without ambient credentials, and outputs cross-checked against .ai/repo-map.generated.md before they are trusted.

checklist: The MCP server or code-graph tool is pinned to an explicit version, tag or commit and approved in the task
It runs sandboxed, without ambient credentials, write access or data sharing beyond the declared scope
Its output is treated as untrusted and cross-checked against .ai/repo-map.generated.md before it guides an edit

rules.title: Concurrent sessions isolate worktrees and respect single-writer surfaces
rules.statement: Parallel agent sessions work in their own .worktrees/<slug> checkout, never edit or prune another session's worktree, and treat generated and lock files as single-writer surfaces that are regenerated rather than hand-merged; pruning removes only clean, merged, old, repo-local worktrees.

checklist: Each task runs in its own .worktrees/<slug> checkout and single-writer surfaces (AGENTS.md, lockfiles, constitution, baseline, generated map/CSS, evidence) are edited by one session at a time
Validation distinguishes your own staged change from another session's dirty worktree and uses the quiet gate (npm run check:agent plus focused tests)
Pruning removes only clean, merged, repo-local worktrees older than the threshold; external, current and nested-parent worktrees are never touched
